pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/lib/prompt-context.ts:118 formatDynamicContext still inlines every scanned class name (and every plugin and Build.cs dependency) with no cap, no floor/elastic split, no degradation ladder and no truncation notice, so a large UE project floods the context layer of every prompt the builder assembles.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/prompt-context.ts:118 The full class list is inlined with no budget, no ladder and no 'N more not shown' notice. Re-checked 2026-11-04: the earlier verdict still holds.

src/lib/prompt-context.ts:147 List variables are rendered as joined strings with no cap, and no variable declares a trust class. Partial credit: a missing required section fails loudly (prompt-builder.ts:233 throws).

src/lib/prompt-context.ts:410 The scanned class list is reachable material, cached at scan time, and `scannedAt` is never rendered. The rules forbid the agent from checking it and line 152 calls it authoritative, so the agent is steered away from verifying a cache that may be stale.

src/lib/prompts/prompt-builder.ts:306 A fluent assembler exists, but the code itself documents hand-rolled prompts that bypass it. withRaw* setters accept pre-rendered text, build() returns an open string, and inside the header the volatile scan and error memory (line 395) come before the stable Rules/policy block.

src/lib/prompts/prompt-builder.ts:271 The assembler returns bare text with no digest of the standing layers. Prompt versions elsewhere are hand-set labels, not fingerprints, so a stale session cannot be detected.

src/types/prompt-evolution.ts:87 The evolution loop's shorten mutation (implemented at src/lib/prompt-evolution/mutations.ts:127) regex-deletes every parenthetical and em-dash aside, which is where hedges and conditions live. Nothing reviews the diff for a deferred decision that the cut resolved.
src/lib/prompt-context.ts:416 The done criterion is a check the model can run against the artifact, not 'verify your answer'. Domain lines are scope statements, not expertise claims.
src/lib/prompt-context.ts:105 No date or time is rendered anywhere in the header (even scannedAt is omitted), so the precondition does not hold.
src/lib/prompts/prompt-builder.ts:4 This builds one prompt per turn with no transcript layer. The Claude CLI owns the history.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/components/cli/skills.ts:248 Skill packs are string-concatenated in front of a prompt that PromptBuilder already assembled, so a whole standing layer enters the model's text outside the assembler's ordering, budget and any fingerprint: the unsealed door the golden path names.

techniques.evidence: src/components/cli/skills.ts:248 Concatenation after assembly. The packs also land ahead of the ## Project Context section, so they are not a section the assembler owns.

src/components/cli/useTaskQueue.ts:951 Any existing session is resumed. Nothing compares the skill set or standing prompt the session was born under with the current one, so the session can go stale after a configuration change.
src/components/cli/skills.ts:239 Skill changes never rewrite a live session's standing text. They take effect when the next session starts.

src/components/cli/useTaskQueue.ts:770 Agent-held regime: the client sends only the new turn plus a resume id. The CLI holds and compacts the transcript, and the client runs no editing or compaction of its own.
src/components/cli/useTaskQueue.ts:832 The interactive path also sends only deltas, so the client never holds a message list to compact.
src/components/cli/skills.ts:210 Skill packs are authored in-repo (SKILL_PACKS). Nothing is installed from an outside author.
